title: Growth Table
body:
Goal: build a table that shows how the number of steps GROWS when the list gets bigger, for linear and binary search.

  1. Open starter.py in Thonny.
  2. Finish linear_worst and halving_steps.
  3. Before you press Run, write your predictions on the homework sheet.
  4. Press Run. You should see:
   items |  linear |  binary
      10 |      10 |       4
     100 |     100 |       7
    1000 |    1000 |      10
 1000000 | 1000000 |      20

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Two functions need work: linear_worst and halving_steps. Read the sentence above each one. Linear search might look at every item, so ask yourself how many items that is. Then look at the TODO 2 note.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: linear_worst(n) only needs to hand back a number it already has. For halving_steps, use a while loop that keeps going as long as n is above 0. Inside it, cut n in half with // and count one more step.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Start with while n ____ 0:. Inside the loop, halve n and count one more step. After the loop, give back steps. Try n = 10 on paper first: 10, then 5, then 2, and keep going until you reach 0.

# Growth Table - YOUR version
# How many steps does each search need in the WORST case?
#   linear search: it may have to look at every item -> n steps
#   binary search: it halves the list until nothing is left
# Finish the TODOs, then press Run and see if it does what the README says.


def linear_worst(n):
    """Worst case for linear search on n items."""
    # TODO 1: linear search may look at every single item. Return that number.
    return 0


def halving_steps(n):
    """How many times can we halve n (keeping whole numbers) until it is 0?
    That is the worst case for binary search on n items."""
    steps = 0
    # TODO 2: while n is more than 0: n = n // 2 and add 1 to steps
    return steps


def growth_table(sizes):
    """Return a list of rows (n, linear steps, binary steps). (Already done!)"""
    rows = []
    for n in sizes:
        rows.append((n, linear_worst(n), halving_steps(n)))
    return rows


def format_row(n, linear, binary):
    """Line up the numbers in columns, e.g. '    1000 |    1000 |      10'."""
    return f"{n:>8} | {linear:>7} | {binary:>7}"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"{'items':>8} | {'linear':>7} | {'binary':>7}")
    for n, linear, binary in growth_table([10, 100, 1000, 1000000]):
        print(format_row(n, linear, binary))
